critical_evidence.evidence: No borescope images or report in the listing or the CARFAX. This 3.4 M97 is the bore-scoring-prone variant, so a borescope is the single most valuable test here.

No IMS retrofit invoice and no engine number. A 2008 M97 would normally carry the larger non-serviceable bearing, but this has to be confirmed by engine number. No reported entry of any clutch or IMS work.
CARFAX shows an oil and filter change at Repair206 on 10/13/2026 (77,503 mi). There is no indication the filter was cut or inspected, and no photo.
No fault memory, cam deviation or over-rev range printout provided.
All attached photos show the top stowed. No top-cycle video, drain photos or footwell photos were examined here.

documentation.rationale: The identity and terms half is strong. The VIN matches the decode, the price is itemised ($27,995 + $200 doc), and a purchased CARFAX shows clean title brands, no reported accidents, 3 owners and a consistent odometer. The maintenance half is nearly empty. Apart from a 2016 Porsche-dealer check-in and a 10/2026 oil change, there is no reported service for about 10 years and 15k miles, and there is no IMS, borescope, cooling or top evidence.

condition.rationale: No fault is stated, and the photos show clean, even paint, clear headlamp lenses, factory wheels and decent-looking Michelins. Nothing proves mechanical condition: no engine bay or underside photos, no scan, no borescope. The roughly 1,700 mi/yr use since 2017 with no reported service means age-related rubber, coolant and seal items are open questions.

price_value.rationale: The asking price of $27,995 ($28,195 with doc fee) sits above the fair-value mid of $27,378 and at the top of the $22,050–$28,166 range. Lower-mileage 2008 S peers ask $29,870 at 45k miles, and a 65k-mile 2008 S asks $25,740. The car brings no documented IMS, borescope or cooling work, which are the items that justify top-of-range money on a 987.1.

mission_fit.rationale: A manual, naturally aspirated mid-engine roadster matches the enthusiast brief and resells easily. However, the M97 3.4's IMS and bore-scoring exposure is a reliability question for a bridge car. The asking price also sits well above the $10,000–$19,000 ideal band, which leaves little margin for the 987.1 catch-up list.

logistics.rationale: Kent, WA is about 746 miles away, a straightforward fly-and-drive. The dealer offers a video walkaround and window sticker, and there are Porsche specialists nearby for a PPI, though PPI access is not yet confirmed. The car's California emissions history (passes in 2014 and 2016) makes CA registration and smog feasible.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Several desirable traits stack up: S model, 6-speed manual, PASM, Sport Chrono Package Plus, bi-xenons and the Windstop, all on a stock-appearing car. Meteor Grey over Stone Grey is attractive but not one of the fastest-selling colours.

ppi_focus: Borescope all six cylinders for scoring, and compare soot colour between the left and right exhaust tips, since one-bank sooting is a scoring tell.
Cut and inspect the oil filter, and check oil consumption history and the oil level on the dipstick or display.
Durametric scan: over-rev ranges (critical on a manual), stored faults, and cam deviation on both banks.
Cold-start listen for piston slap or ticking and a 1–3 second chain/Variocam rattle, and watch for startup smoke (AOS).
Underside check for an active RMS/IMS-area drip at the bellhousing, and look for evidence of any prior engine-out work.
Cooling system: water pump weep, expansion tank cracks and pink crust, and coolant hose condition. Remove the front grilles and inspect the radiators and condensers for debris packing and corrosion.
Cycle the convertible top repeatedly, check the cables, drive blocks and hydraulic rams for leaks, and pull the footwell and under-seat carpet edges for water staining.
Clutch engagement point and DMF judder from a stop. Confirm the manual gearbox shifts cleanly through all six gears.
Front lower control arms, coffin-arm bushings, top mounts and tie rods, and check that PASM functions without faults.
Tire date codes, paint meter readings on all panels (given the 2016 'reconditioned' entry), and a check of the maritime-climate underside and fasteners.
what_would_change_verdict: Up: a clean borescope of all six cylinders, a clean filter cut and a Durametric printout with no meaningful over-revs would retire the largest M97 risks.
Up: invoices from 2017–2026, especially water pump, coolant tank and condenser work, or an engine number confirming bearing type plus any IMS/clutch receipts.
Up: a price negotiation toward the fair-value mid that reflects the undocumented cooling and IMS items.
Down: any scoring on the borescope, metal in the filter, significant over-rev counts, or the dealer refusing an independent PPI before a deposit.
Down: evidence of an active RMS/IMS leak, coolant loss, top or drain water damage, or old tires adding known work.
evidence.mission_note: A manual 3.4 S with PASM and Sport Chrono fits the enthusiast-bridge brief and is easy to resell. However, the M97's IMS and bore-scoring exposure and a decade of unreported maintenance make its reliability as a bridge car unproven until a borescope and scan are done. The accelerated_bridge mode does not justify skipping that inspection.
evidence.rationale: The purchased CARFAX establishes the car's identity and title cleanly: the VIN matches, there are no DMV damage or odometer brands, no reported accidents, three owners (two in California, one in Washington for nearly nine years), and a consistent odometer trail to 77,503 miles. The photos show a stock-appearing, well-presented Meteor Grey car on factory wheels with matching Michelin tires. Nothing is observed wrong. However, the document shows no reported service entry for about ten years and 15k miles (05/2016 to 10/2026) beyond a pre-sale oil change, and use was very light during that period. None of the six model-critical items is evidenced: no borescope, no IMS or engine-number evidence, no filter cut, no scan, no top video and no cooling receipts. That matters most on the 3.4 M97, the bore-scoring-prone engine. The asking price of $27,995 plus a $200 doc fee sits slightly above the $27,378 fair-value mid and at the top of the estimated range. The open questions are mechanical and answerable through a specialist PPI and the dealer's records.
evidence.next_action: Call Unique Motors and ask three things: the engine number, the Repair206 invoice, and written agreement to an independent PPI with a borescope and Durametric scan at a Seattle-area Porsche specialist before any deposit.
